answer:
Here's the audit. I ran the memory system's consolidation scan (read-only — nothing was changed) across everything tagged `atlas`, which covered 120 stored claims. I then manually checked the flagged pairs, since the automated similarity scan surfaces "topically related" pairs as well as true duplicates/contradictions, and those need to be told apart.

## Real duplicates (same fact, restated) — worth merging
- **Test runner**: "The atlas test suite is run with `cargo nextest run`, not `cargo test`" and "Tests in atlas are run through `cargo nextest run`; plain `cargo test` is not used" — identical claim, two entries.
- **Deploy command**: three separate entries all say the same thing — "Project atlas is deployed by running `bin/ship.sh` from the repository root," "To ship atlas you run the `bin/ship.sh` script at the top of the repo," and "Deploying atlas means executing `bin/ship.sh`; the old `make deploy` target is gone." The third adds one new detail (old `make deploy` retired) worth keeping when merged.

## Real contradiction — needs a decision before handover
- **Staging deploy trigger**: one memory says *"Merging to main deploys atlas to staging automatically"*; another says *"Deploys to atlas staging are never automatic: someone runs `bin/ship.sh --staging` by hand."* These directly conflict. The automated scan didn't even pair these two together (it linked the second one to an unrelated ship.sh entry instead) — I only caught it by cross-reading. Whoever inherits this needs to know which is actually true.
- **"Feature flags" — likely two different things conflated**: "Feature flags in atlas are an environment variable map and nothing more" vs. "Feature flags in atlas are additive only, so `cargo check --all-features` has to pass." The second is clearly about Cargo compile-time feature flags; the first sounds like runtime config. Same term, two different mechanisms — worth disambiguating so a new owner doesn't assume they're the same system.

## Stale / time-bound notes that have outlived their relevance
- "The branch under review is spike/consolidate." — filed as short-lived, untouched for 40 days, about to expire on its own. No longer meaningful.
- "The flaky test being chased this week is `pagination_ordering` in atlas-api." — the "this week" framing is ~40 days stale. Either it's long since fixed or still flaky and should be re-filed as a durable fact, not left as an expiring scratch note.

## Automated noise — flagging so you're not surprised, no action needed
The consolidator grouped 8 unrelated facts as "near-duplicates" (license, GitHub Discussions for feature requests, repo access owner, no job queue, npm SDK name, TS+Python SDK list, OpenAPI generation, deprecated-endpoint policy) — its own output admits this chained together through weak middle-similarity links rather than being one real duplicate cluster. Same for a few "contradiction" pairs it surfaced (e.g. GHCR image push vs. distroless base image; connection-pool-size-16 vs. readiness-probe-waits-on-pool) — these are just topically adjacent, not conflicting or duplicated.

Nothing has been changed. Want me to merge the confirmed duplicates and resolve the two contradictions (asking you which staging-deploy behavior and feature-flag meaning is current), and clear out the two stale notes?
